document.title: Edit check
document.attribution: MediaWiki.org contributors and the Wikimedia Foundation Editing team

individuals.title: Edit Check
individuals.description: The visual editor's ability to check the change someone is making and offer actionable feedback about Wikipedia policies while they edit.

evidence.quote: Offer people actionable feedback about Wikipedia policies while they are editing.
will check the changes people are attempting to make and present them with actions they can take to improve these changes

individuals.title: Reference Check
individuals.description: The first check: detects new content added without a reference and prompts the editor to add one.

evidence.quote: The first "check" the Editing Team will be introducing is one that will detect when people are attempting to add *new* content to an existing article *without* a corresponding reference and prompt them to do so.
- **Reference check**

individuals.title: Link check and Reference reliability
individuals.description: A check on the links and the reliability of the references an editor adds; listed among the available features.

evidence.quote: - **Link check and Reference reliability**

individuals.title: Paste Check
individuals.description: A check on pasted content; listed among the available features.

evidence.quote: - **Paste Check**

individuals.title: Tone Check
individuals.description: A new check the Editing team is working on.

evidence.quote: - **Tone check**

individuals.title: Multi-Check
individuals.description: Showing several Reference Checks within a single editing session.

evidence.quote: Multi-Check caused statistically significant increases in the proportion of edits that include a reference
multiple reference checks were shown within a single editing session

individuals.title: Suggestion Mode
individuals.description: A related feature that presents suggestions on existing article content; available as a Beta Feature.

evidence.quote: The team is continuing to work on Suggestion Mode. The feature has been available as a Beta Feature globally since early March
- **Suggestion Mode**

individuals.title: TextMatch
individuals.description: A related feature communities use to create custom local types of Suggestion.

evidence.quote: Some communities have started to use the textMatch feature to create custom local types of Suggestion.
- **TextMatch**

evidence.quote: The team is building a way for Suggestions to be stored more efficiently

individuals.title: Newcomers feel safe and confident publishing changes they are proud of
individuals.description: Objective 1: newcomers and Junior Contributors from Sub-Saharan Africa feel safe and confident enough to publish changes they are proud of and that experienced volunteers find useful.

evidence.quote: Newcomers and Junior Contributors from Sub-Saharan Africa will feel safe and confident enough while editing to publish changes they are proud of and that experienced volunteers consider useful.

individuals.title: Moderators see better newcomer edits and configure Edit Check
individuals.description: Objective 2: moderators at the English and French Wikipedias notice better newcomer edits and are motivated to configure how Edit Check presents policies.

evidence.quote: Moderators at the English and French Wikipedias will notice improvements in the quality of edits newcomers are making and be motivated to configure how Edit Check presents policies to them.

individuals.title: Make existing norms legible and actionable while editing
individuals.description: Make the norms and standards currently in place legible and actionable to people while they are editing.

evidence.quote: we first need to make the norms and standards that are currently in place legible and actionable to people while they are editing

individuals.title: Policies and content reflect the diverse experiences of the people served
individuals.description: The longer-term future the project works toward: wikis' policies, norms and content reflect the diverse experiences of the people they serve.

evidence.quote: to evolve towards a future where wikis' policies and cultural norms – and ultimately, content – reflect the diverse experiences of the people these projects are intended to serve

individuals.title: Higher quality of newcomer edits in the main namespace
individuals.description: Intended impact 1: increase the quality of the edits newcomers and Junior Contributors in Sub-Saharan Africa publish in the main namespace.

evidence.quote: Increase the quality of edits newcomers and Junior Contributors editing from within Sub-Saharan Africa publish in the main namespace

individuals.title: Newcomers accompany new content with a reference
individuals.description: Intended impact 2: increase the likelihood that newcomers and Junior Contributors accompany new content with a reference.

evidence.quote: Increase the likelihood that newcomers and Junior Contributors editing from within Sub-Saharan Africa will accompany the new content they are adding with a reference

individuals.title: Newcomers report feeling safe and confident
individuals.description: Intended impact 3: newcomers and Junior Contributors report feeling safe and confident making changes to Wikipedia.

evidence.quote: Newcomers and Junior Contributors editing from within Sub-Saharan Africa will report feeling safe and confident making changes to Wikipedia

individuals.title: Experienced volunteers audit and iterate on the default configurations
individuals.description: Intended impact 4: experienced volunteers independently audit and iterate on Edit Check's default configurations.

evidence.quote: Experienced volunteers will independently audit and iterate upon Edit Check's default configurations to ensure Edit Check is causing newcomers and Junior Contributors to make productive edits.

individuals.title: Newcomers are more aware of the need to add a reference
individuals.description: Intended impact 5: newcomers and Junior Contributors are more aware of the need to add a reference because the visual editor prompts them.

evidence.quote: Newcomers and Junior Contributors will be more aware of the need to add a reference when contributing new content because the visual editor will prompt them to do so

individuals.title: Editing interfaces do not make people aware of policies
individuals.description: The gap the project responds to: the visual editor and other editing interfaces do not make people aware of the policies and guidelines they are expected to follow.

evidence.quote: The trouble is that the visual editor and other editing interfaces do not make people aware of the Wikipedia policies and guidelines they are expected to follow.

individuals.title: Good-faith newcomer edits are reverted and newcomers leave
individuals.description: Inexperienced volunteers become disappointed and frustrated when their good-faith changes are undone, which drives them away.

evidence.quote: become disappointed and frustrated when the good-faith change(s) they arrived to the wiki seeking to make are undone (read: reverted), deleted, and/or scrutinized in inequitable ways

individuals.title: Moderation burden on experienced volunteers
individuals.description: Experienced volunteers must do more work reverting low-quality edits and educating newcomers, which makes them sceptical and impatient.

evidence.quote: Continually needing to educate inexperienced volunteers and undo their changes can lead to experienced volunteers becoming skeptical of inexperienced volunteers and impatient with them.

individuals.title: Wikipedia projects struggle to grow and diversify their volunteers
individuals.description: The projects struggle to grow and diversify their volunteer populations and to shrink knowledge gaps.

evidence.quote: struggle to grow and diversify their volunteer populations and shrink the knowledge gaps present within Wikimedia wikis

individuals.title: Difficulty retaining editors outside Europe and North America
individuals.description: The movement struggles to retain editors who live outside Europe and North America.

evidence.quote: The movement struggles to retain editors who live outside Europe and North America.

individuals.title: People from Sub-Saharan Africa are underrepresented among editors
individuals.description: People from Sub-Saharan Africa are 1% of active editors but 15% of the world's population and 7% of its internet population.

evidence.quote: people from Sub-Saharan Africa represent only 1% of active unique editors, despite representing 15% of the global population and 7% of the global internet population

individuals.title: Reference Check A/B test
individuals.description: The finding that Reference Check raised the quality of newcomers' edits without significant disruption (2.2 times more constructive edits with a reference; revert rate down 8.6%).

evidence.quote: Reference Check caused an **increase in the quality of edits** newcomers publish and **did not cause any significant disruption**.
People shown the Reference Check are **2.2 times more likely** to publish a new content edit that includes a reference and is constructive (not reverted within 48 hours).

individuals.title: Multi-Check (References) A/B test
individuals.description: The finding that Multi-Check significantly raised the share of edits that include a reference and are not reverted, without harming edit completion.

evidence.quote: Multi-Check caused statistically significant increases in the proportion of edits that include a reference and are not reverted within 48 hours without causing undesirable changes in edit completion or other forms of disruption (e.g. blocks).

individuals.title: Multi-Check Phase 1 impact analysis
individuals.description: The before-and-after finding that moving checks to the desktop siderail was net positive (revert rate down 15.7%).

evidence.quote: The findings above suggest this design change has been net positive.
The revert rate of new content edits where Reference Check was activated decreased by **15.7%**.

individuals.title: LLMs can evaluate whether sources corroborate claims (English)
individuals.description: Research confirmed that, in English, LLMs are effective at evaluating whether web-based sources corroborate claims on Wikipedia.

evidence.quote: This research confirmed that in English LLMs are effective at evaluating whether web-based sources corroborate claims on Wikipedia.
